page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations.

This virtual machine is provisioned with 945 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage options. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware configuration lacks dedicated GPU accelerators, meaning all computational tasks rely entirely on the host CPU.

Performance benchmarks place the D16ds_v6 in the average range for most operations. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1771.0 and a multi-core score of 10861.0. In memory bandwidth tests, it recorded 1035.16 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 105.59 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The system demonstrates strong performance in specific workloads, such as text generation for a small 135M parameter language model, reaching 292.48 tokens/sec. However, larger model inference is constrained, with a 7B model yielding 14.67 tokens/sec for text generation. Redis SET operations reached 19.51 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was measured at 24.09 GB/sec.

The D16ds_v6 offers a balanced resource profile, combining dedicated CPU cores, a substantial local disk, and standard memory density. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, relational databases, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks.
